messages.author: eb8f81cb4d55140d
messages.subject: Posterior for spatial averages
parts:
Hello,

I am working with a GLMM with spatial effects

Y(s)|\mu(s) ~ Gamma(\mu(s) , \phi)
log(\mu(s)) = X(s)\beta + u(s)

where Y(s) is the response of interest at location s, X(s) are known covariates and u(s) is the latent spatial effect. Model fitting with INLA went smoothly as well as predictions at a set of locations s_1, ..., s_N. 

But I am interested in the posterior of the average value of Y(s) within a given area, approximated by the finite sum over my prediction locations: (1/N) \sum Y(s_i).

It seems to me this unavoidably requires the joint posterior for Y(s_i), or u(s_i), for i = 1, .., N. The number of prediction locations is large, N ~ 10^7.

Is there a good way to do this?

Thanks,
Paul

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Posterior for spatial averages
parts:
For those kinds of predictions, posterior sampling with inla.posterior.sample() is easiest; the samples are based on the joint posterior approximation, so you can compute any functional of the samples to get a sample from the posterior distribution of those functionals.
Finn

messages.author: 8c8975f95cb8f4df
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Posterior for spatial averages
parts:
Hi Finn and Paul

This is very useful. We implemented it in a small example and it worked fine. However, in our analysis we have factorial parameters, smoothers and a SRF. This complicates the coding and we would appreciate some help on this.

Below is the relevant parts of our code boiled down to three years (the factor) and one smoother (Depth_m) and the SRF.

We think that we must feed in the prediction values for factors and smoothers in a special way in ‘fun’, but how to code this?

Kind regards

Søren and Teunis

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The smoothers are made like this:

#'  We will use an unpenalized cubic regression spline with 3 knots.

#'  Depth smoother: f(Depth) = XDepth * beta

Lego.Depth_m <- smoothCon(s(Depth_m, bs = "cr", k = 3, fx = TRUE),

                          data = dfModelData, 

                          absorb.cons = TRUE)[[1]]

 #' Extract the X matrix.

XDepth_m <- Lego.Depth_m$X  #X for the Depth smoother

 #' It is needed as a data frame for the lincomb.

XDepth_m.df <- data.frame(XDepth_m)

 #' Add column names to the data frame.

names(XDepth_m.df) <- paste0("XDepth_m", 1:ncol(XDepth_m))

 #' Define the linear combination XDepth * beta.

lcs.Depth_m <- inla.make.lincombs(XDepth_m.df)

#Rename

names(lcs.Depth_m) <- paste(names(lcs.Depth_m), "Depth_m", sep = "")

#Select the smoothers that should be used.

lcs <- c(lcs.Depth_m)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Then we make a mesh, a stack etc,

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# and the formula:

formulaGAM_YearlySRF <- formula(ResponseVar ~ -1 + Intercept +

 fYear2016 + fYear2017 +                                           #The three years 2015-2017 as factors

                XDepth_m +                                                                 # The depth smoother

                f(w, model = spde.holes, replicate = w.repl))      #The SRF

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#Fit the model:

fitNegBin_GAM_YearlySRF <- inla(formulaGAM_YearlySRF,

                                lincomb = lcs,#lcs.Depth_m,

                                family = "nbinomial",

                                data = inla.stack.data(StackHoles, spde = spde.holes),

                                control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, config=TRUE),

                                control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(StackHoles)))

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

And then we come to the prediction part of the code:

We have already made a prediction data.frame called dfDataPredict with combinations of Years, Depths and spatial positions.

Then we sample:

INLA_Samples_fitNegBin_GAM_YearlySRF = inla.posterior.sample(1000, fitNegBin_GAM_YearlySRF)

And:

fun = function(dfDataPredict = NA) {

 return (Intercept + fYear2016 + fYear2017 + XDepth_m

+ f(w, model = spde.holes, replicate = w.repl))

 }

 lstPredictions = inla.posterior.sample.eval(fun, INLA_Samples_fitNegBin_GAM_YearlySRF,

                                            dfPredictionData=dfPredictionData)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
